mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 2.5% in a given month coincides with a short-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE by at least 0.2 percentage points is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as lower labor market tightness reduces wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: In regimes with rising employment (PAYEMS > 1.2M), the effect is not statistically significant (Rank IC < 0.05 over 60 days).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (units of new home sales) above the prior month's level coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220), the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 20-day return (paired t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (index of industrial production) of at least 2% followed by a rebound above the low suggests cyclical bottoming, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market expectations for growth improve.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO two consecutive monthly declines of >= 2%, then rebound above low
failure_condition: No significant improvement in SPX 20-day forward returns within 4 weeks of the rebound (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 both show simultaneous monthly increases, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is more positive than when either moves alone, reflecting coordinated easing and stronger demand.
candidate_trigger: Both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 month-over-month increases
failure_condition: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220), the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.1 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS (number of payroll jobs) of at least 50,000 for three consecutive months is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as rising labor market slack reduces hiring confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month decline >= 50,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of falling unemployment (UNRATE < 4%), the effect is not observed (Rank IC < 0.05 over 60 days).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly RSAFS (retail sales) reading above 400,000 million dollars in a deflationary regime (CPIAUCSL < 210) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it indicates resilient consumer spending despite low inflation.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 400,000M and CPIAUCSL < 210 in a given month
failure_condition: In periods of high uncertainty (UNRATE > 6%), the interaction is not predictive (p > 0.1 in F-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (CPI YoY) of at least 3% followed by a sustained 2-month plateau is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals a moderation in price pressures that supports valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month drop >= 3%, followed by 2 months of plateau
failure_condition: No significant forward return in periods of simultaneous high inflation and weak GDP growth (GDPC1 < 10,000 and INDPRO < 105).
